newsitem.title: USA: Texas "Cheerleader Mom" released from jail.
newsitem.headline: Texas "Cheerleader Mom" released from jail.

text.p: A Texas woman who was convicted of trying to hire a hitman to kill the mother of her daughter's cheerleader rival was released from jail on Friday after nearly six months behind bars.

Wanda Holloway, who became known as the "Cheerleader Mom" in a case that drew worldwide attention, will remain on probation but must perform 1,000 hours of community service and undergo psychiatric testing, said state District Judge George Godwin.

Holloway was found guilty in 1991 of plotting to have friend and neighbour Verna Heath killed. Holloway hoped Heath's daughter, Amber, would become so upset she would quit the cheerleading squad at a junior high in the Houston suburb of Channelview, Texas, opening up a spot for Holloway's daughter Shanna.
The plot fell apart when the would-be hitman went to police.
The 1991 conviction, which resulted in a 15-year jail sentence, was thrown out because a member of the jury was found to have a criminal record.
In a plea agreement worked out last September, Holloway pleaded no contest in exchange for a 10-year probated sentence that included a brief jail term.
